practice_claim: Before adopting any token-reduction transform on code shown to the agent (minification, comment/whitespace stripping, learned or continuous-latent compression), measure the end-task cost, and adopt only where the token budget genuinely binds. If repository context must be compressed, stay at mild ratios (~4x) and validate on generation and cross-file tasks, not just completion.
boundary_conditions: Measured on specific pipelines and models; re-measure per agent, task mix, and compression method. Aggressive compression is unsafe for tasks that depend on cross-file relational structure, and completion-task validation alone will overstate safety.
citation: Nicolas Hrubec, Jürgen Cito (2026). Reducing Token Usage of State-in-Context Agents using Minification. arXiv:2606.01326.
claim_support: 42% token savings from minification cost 12 pp of SWE-bench Verified resolution; token-reduction transforms are not free.

claim_support: At ~4x compression continuous-latent methods can beat full context (up to +28.3% BLEU); token-level methods converge to no-context performance at 7-12x on generation tasks; visual rendering loses cross-file structure at any resolution.

practice_claim: Build rules files up gradually from real need and keep them small; move everything else into path-scoped rules, on-demand skills, and subagents that load only when relevant, and operate below the model's 'dumb zone' through intentional compaction.
boundary_conditions: Sharing context configurations works far better inside a team than between strangers; there are no unit tests for context engineering, so a configuration must be lived with before it can be judged; models improve, so last year's necessary context may now be dead weight. Where the 'dumb zone' begins varies by model and task and is stated without measurement. The restart-on-appeasement heuristic that previously rode along here has been dropped: single anecdotal source, no measurement, and a different mechanism from context sizing.
citation: "Context Engineering for Coding Agents", Birgitta Böckeler (Thoughtworks), published on martinfowler.com, 2026-02-05.
claim_support: Keep always-loaded rules small and grown from real need; lazy-load the rest via path-scoped rules, skills, and subagents; copied configs cause contradictory instructions.

practice_claim: Before building any metric, manually review 100+ diverse raw traces with open-ended notes, annotate only the first upstream failure in each trace, cluster the notes into 5-10 themes, and aim the first mitigations at the phases/classes where the failure mass concentrates (planning and self-diagnosis in published base rates).
boundary_conditions: Manual review does not scale (that is what a validated judge is for afterward) and needs a domain expert plus a trace viewer. The published phase distribution comes from 34 programmable tasks on off-the-shelf frameworks at ~50% completion, not frontier coding agents; category boundaries blur on long multi-phase tasks.
citation: Ruofan Lu, Yichen Li, Yintong Huo (2025). Exploring Autonomous Agents: A Closer Look at Why They Fail When Completing Tasks. arXiv:2508.13143.
claim_support: Phase-aligned failure classification (planning/execution/response); mitigation advice targets the phases with the highest observed failure share.

claim_support: Open coding on 100+ traces, annotate first upstream failure, axial coding into 5-10 themes, prioritize by frequency; pre-built metrics uncorrelated with outcomes.

claim_support: The interaction-centered taxonomy organizes 41 failure modes, and its strongest automated judge reached Cohen's kappa of 0.76 against human labels. The agreement result supports label reproducibility, not causal correctness or the chapter's local derivation protocol.

practice_claim: Impose a turn/iteration budget on agent loops: fixed at roughly the 75th percentile of the unrestricted baseline's turn distribution, or better, a small default budget with on-demand extensions, plus explicit exit conditions and backoff/fallback handling for flaky dependencies, rather than letting runs go unbounded.
boundary_conditions: Percentile must be recalibrated per scaffold/model/task mix; a hard cap converts some slow successes into failures (the dynamic strategy softens that edge); caps that are too tight truncate legitimate long tasks. The practitioner account is vendor-adjacent marketing. Splitting a fixed budget across stages of a sequential workflow has a closed-form answer (give more tokens to the stages whose reliability saturates slowest, equalizing marginal gain per token), but it is theory plus numerical illustration and it needs per-agent reliability curves that nobody in this catalog reports measuring. Cap first; allocate analytically only once you have those curves.
citation: Pengfei Gao, Chao Peng (2025). More with Less: An Empirical Study of Turn-Control Strategies for Efficient Coding Agents. arXiv:2510.16786.
claim_support: 75th-percentile turn caps cut costs 24-68% with minimal solve-rate impact; dynamic extension beat fixed caps by 12-24%.

citation: Ya-Ting Yang, Quanyan Zhu (2026). Toward Reliable Design of LLM-Enabled Agentic Workflows: Optimizing Latency-Reliability-Cost Tradeoffs. arXiv:2605.23929.

practice_claim: Select detection methods by access level (training data: matching; logits: NLL/Min-K and order-canonicity tests; text only: prompting probes) and suspected channel (verbatim, paraphrase, cross-lingual); always run more than one, and never certify a closed model clean because detectors came back negative.
boundary_conditions: Order-canonicity requires log-probability access and misses contamination that preserved exchangeability; detectors were validated on early base models and transfer poorly to instruction-tuned frontier models, especially for fine-tuning-stage contamination with answer augmentation; adversarial evasion bounds what detection can promise — detector disagreement itself is a flag for manual audit.
citation: Yonatan Oren, Nicole Meister, Niladri Chatterji, Faisal Ladhak, Tatsunori B. Hashimoto (2023). Proving Test Set Contamination in Black Box Language Models. arXiv:2310.17623.
claim_support: Canonical-order vs shuffled log-probability comparison yields provable contamination evidence from log-probs alone, sensitive even to datasets seen a few times in pretraining.

practice_claim: Detect implicit reward hacking by measuring reasoning effort: truncate the CoT at increasing lengths, force an answer at each cut, and flag runs where high reward is reached with a small fraction of the reasoning (large truncated-reward AUC).
boundary_conditions: Requires the ability to fork/truncate reasoning and re-sample answers (harness access, extra compute); calibration of 'suspiciously early' is task-dependent; reported gains (>65% over a 72B CoT monitor) are on their evaluation suite.
citation: Xinpeng Wang, Nitish Joshi, Barbara Plank, Rico Angell, He He (2025). Is It Thinking or Cheating? Detecting Implicit Reward Hacking by Measuring Reasoning Effort. arXiv:2510.01367.
claim_support: Truncated-reward AUC detects hacking without reading CoT content; robust to obfuscation.

practice_claim: Before acting on a benchmark ranking, re-run it under perturbation — semantically transformed problem variants (difficulty-shifted, recombined, rephrased) and harness perturbations (answer-choice reordering, alternative scoring methods) — and treat rank shifts under perturbation as the ranking's real uncertainty.
boundary_conditions: LLM transformation can drift task difficulty, so absolute scores on evolved sets are not comparable to originals; validated at function level and on multiple-choice benchmarks — for generative/agentic tasks the analogous perturbation variables are grader and scaffold choices.
citation: Chunqiu Steven Xia, Yinlin Deng, Lingming Zhang (2024). Top Leaderboard Ranking = Top Coding Proficiency, Always? EvoEval: Evolving Coding Benchmarks via LLM. arXiv:2403.19114.
claim_support: LLM-evolved HumanEval variants dropped scores ~39% on average and reordered leaderboard positions, exposing surface-form overfitting.

practice_claim: Before acting on a benchmark ranking, re-run it under perturbation — semantically transformed problem variants (difficulty-shifted, recombined, rephrased) and harness perturbations (answer-choice reordering, alternative scoring methods) — and treat rank shifts under perturbation as the ranking's real uncertainty.
boundary_conditions: LLM transformation can drift task difficulty, so absolute scores on evolved sets are not comparable to originals; validated at function level and on multiple-choice benchmarks — for generative/agentic tasks the analogous perturbation variables are grader and scaffold choices.
citation: Norah Alzahrani, Hisham Abdullah Alyahya, Yazeed Alnumay, Sultan Alrashed, Shaykhah Alsubaie, et al. (2024). When Benchmarks are Targets: Revealing the Sensitivity of Large Language Model Leaderboards. arXiv:2402.01781.
claim_support: MMLU-style rankings move up to 8 positions under minute evaluation-design changes (answer reordering, scoring method); prefer hybrid scoring and treat rank shifts as ranking uncertainty.

practice_claim: When using LLMs for error attribution at all, structure the trace into hierarchical context levels and aggregate multiple independent judge passes by consensus or confidence-aware weighting, feeding disagreement back to adapt the judge, instead of one all-at-once read or binary search over the trace.
boundary_conditions: Author-run evaluations on multi-agent interaction scenarios; consensus multiplies inference cost; still subject to the attribution ceiling (see keep-humans-in-failure-attribution); the 'earliest irreversible step' framing fits gradual-degradation cases poorly. AgentLocate is a new preprint with zero external citations yet.
citation: Adi Banerjee, Anirudh Nair, Tarik Borogovac (2025). Where Did It All Go Wrong? A Hierarchical Look into Multi-Agent Error Attribution. arXiv:2510.04886.
claim_support: Hierarchical context leveling plus consensus voting outperformed all-at-once, step-by-step, and binary-search attribution.

practice_claim: Build a read-only replay harness over your own recorded arrival traces (arrival time, priority, claim, duration, outcome, review verdict) and replay identical traces under competing dispatch policies with arrivals held fixed; require any proposed optimizer to beat FCFS and a trivially-tuned priority sort on the same traces, keep a random-oversampling baseline in the protocol, and validate kernels on constructed instances with known optima.
boundary_conditions: Requires ledgers that already capture arrivals/claims/outcomes; per-class starvation must be checked, since a policy can improve the mean by starving one class; measured gains concentrated in genuinely contended pools — gains claimed from uncontended traffic are suspect. Support is three synthesis-synthesis items over external works (Decima 2018arXiv181001963M, SWAY 2016arXiv160807617C, Las Cumbres ILP 2015arXiv150307170L); only SWAY is software-engineering in-domain, and every number quoted above comes from the author's own unpublished 11-week fleet replay, which is held as corroboration and is not a second source.
citation: Hongzi Mao, Malte Schwarzkopf, Shaileshh Bojja Venkatakrishnan, Zili Meng, Mohammad Alizadeh (2018). Learning Scheduling Algorithms for Data Processing Clusters. arXiv:1810.01963.
claim_support: Decima learns cluster scheduling policies with RL and reports that off-the-shelf RL could not handle continuous stochastic job arrivals, so the authors developed training methods specifically for that regime; the prototype on a 25-node Spark cluster beat hand-tuned heuristics by at least 21% average job completion time and up to 2x at high load. The transfer this entry makes - hold the arrival sequence fixed so a run difference is attributable to policy rather than to arrival variance - is an inference in this catalog, drawn from Decima's arrival handling and from simulator-replay practice in survey-telescope operations. Audited 2026-07-27 (evidence audit, evidence audit): Decima's measured result is learned scheduling under stochastic arrivals, not fixed-arrival replay, and the transfer is an inference in this catalog by this note's own admission; regraded directional on that basis.

citation: Jianfeng Chen, Vivek Nair, Rahul Krishna, Tim Menzies (2016). "Sampling"' as a Baseline Optimizer for Search-based Software Engineering. arXiv:1608.07617.
claim_support: SWAY starts from a very large population and samples down to the better solutions rather than evolving generations; across several software-engineering models it was competitive with state-of-the-art evolutionary algorithms at far lower compute cost, and the paper proposes it explicitly as a baseline method for search-based software engineering, especially for slow-to-execute models. This is the in-domain half of the practice: a candidate optimizer that cannot beat a cheap baseline has not earned adoption.

citation: Sotiria Lampoudi, Eric Saunders, Jason Eastman (2015). An Integer Linear Programming Solution to the Telescope Network Scheduling Problem. arXiv:1503.07170.
claim_support: The paper derives a solvable integer-linear-programming model for scheduling a telescope network from the Reservation formalism and reports computational results verifying its correctness plus a Gurobi implementation that handles problems of realistic size. What it supports here is validating a scheduling kernel against instances whose optimum is known before trusting it on live traces; the 'constructed fixtures' phrasing is an inference in this catalog. The The same paper also supports the related practice formalize-work-as-constraints-and-solve-globally.

practice_claim: Build retrieval chunks by recursively splitting large AST nodes and merging small sibling nodes under a size budget, so every chunk is a self-contained syntactic unit; do not use fixed-line-window chunking.
boundary_conditions: Requires a parser per language; gains are at chunking-policy scale (single-digit points) and cannot compensate for a wrong retriever or missing index.
citation: Yilin Zhang, Xinran Zhao, Zora Zhiruo Wang, Chenyang Yang, Jiayi Wei, et al. (2025). cAST: Enhancing Code Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Structural Chunking via Abstract Syntax Tree. arXiv:2506.15655.
claim_support: AST-boundary chunking raised Recall@5 +4.3 (RepoEval) and Pass@1 +2.67 (SWE-bench) over line-window chunking, across languages.

practice_claim: Run the same protocol on matched tasks the benchmark never used — a matched control set, a from-scratch private mirror matched on difficulty, or a retro-holdout twin validated by statistical indistinguishability gates — and report the public-private score gap as the inflation estimate.
boundary_conditions: Requires a genuinely matched control (same language, difficulty, task shape) — mismatched controls confound the gap with difficulty; matched mirrors are expensive (far more so for SWE tasks than math problems) and start leaking on release; retro-holdouts are valid only for models whose cutoff predates the twin's web availability and are demonstrated on QA, not repository-scale coding. Inflation is not uniform across models: GSM1k found many frontier models showed minimal signs of overfitting and all models generalized to the novel items, so a large public-private gap is a per-model signal, not a blanket discount on the leaderboard. The SWE-Bench-Verified comparison is observational, matched only at the level of popular open-source Python projects.
citation: Thanosan Prathifkumar, Noble Saji Mathews, Meiyappan Nagappan (2025). Does SWE-Bench-Verified Test Agent Ability or Model Memory?. arXiv:2512.10218.
claim_support: ~3x overall and ~6x file-localization advantage on SWE-Bench-Verified versus matched BeetleBox/SWE-rebench tasks — a contamination signal human task-screening does nothing to remove.

citation: Hugh Zhang, Jeff Da, Dean Lee, Vaughn Robinson, Catherine Wu, et al. (2024). A Careful Examination of Large Language Model Performance on Grade School Arithmetic. arXiv:2405.00332.
claim_support: GSM1k private mirror revealed up to 8% accuracy drops with systematic overfitting; gap correlated (Spearman r^2 = 0.36) with probability of generating GSM8k items verbatim.

practice_claim: Before publishing or acting on internal eval results, review the pipeline against the 44 catalogued questionable research practices (selective baseline choice, test-set peeking via repeated iteration, cherry-picked checkpoints, unreported prompt tuning) and the irreproducible-practice list.
boundary_conditions: A taxonomy/position paper — it identifies failure modes with examples but does not quantify their prevalence or individual effect sizes.
citation: Gavin Leech, Juan J. Vazquez, Niclas Kupper, Misha Yagudin, Laurence Aitchison (2024). Questionable practices in machine learning. arXiv:2407.12220.
claim_support: 44-item catalog of questionable ML research practices; inflation accumulates from individually defensible choices that all lean one way.

practice_claim: Treat decoding configuration (greedy vs. sampling, temperature, best-of-N) as a first-class experimental variable: report it in the methods, and evaluate under both greedy and sampled generation before claiming a model comparison.
boundary_conditions: Direction of the gap is task-dependent (sampling won on AlpacaEval); alignment methods shrink sampling variance inconsistently, so the gap must be re-measured per model family rather than assumed.
citation: Yifan Song, Guoyin Wang, Sujian Li, Bill Yuchen Lin (2024). The Good, The Bad, and The Greedy: Evaluation of LLMs Should Not Ignore Non-Determinism. arXiv:2407.10457.
claim_support: Greedy-vs-sampling gap is consistent across sizes and large enough to reorder comparisons; task-dependent direction makes undeclared decoding a hidden confound.

practice_claim: When quantifying contamination, choose the contamination metric by whether models actually benefit from the samples it marks contaminated (score delta on marked vs unmarked), instead of reporting raw overlap percentages.
boundary_conditions: Benefit estimation needs enough marked samples for statistical power; effects are model-size dependent (larger models benefit more from less overlap), so conclusions do not transfer across scales.
citation: Aaditya K. Singh, Muhammed Yusuf Kocyigit, Andrew Poulton, David Esiobu, Maria Lomeli, et al. (2024). Evaluation data contamination in LLMs: how do we measure it and (when) does it matter?. arXiv:2411.03923.
claim_support: Benefit-anchored contamination metrics make different contamination definitions comparable and filter out overlap with no score effect; benefit is model-size dependent.

practice_claim: Require the reviewer to commit a judgment before seeing the agent's answer, or delay/slow the reveal at high-stakes checkpoints; aim these scrutiny mechanisms at the fast accept-loop where the programmer already 'knows' the plan, not uniformly across exploration-mode use.
boundary_conditions: Forcing reduced but did not eliminate overreliance; the most effective interventions were rated least favorable, and benefits accrued disproportionately to high Need-for-Cognition users. Acceleration/exploration split observed at suggestion level; transfer to autonomous-agent diffs untested.
citation: Zana Buçinca, Maja Barbara Malaya, Krzysztof Z. Gajos (2021). To Trust or to Think: Cognitive Forcing Functions Can Reduce Overreliance on AI in AI-assisted Decision-making. arXiv:2102.09692.
claim_support: Cognitive forcing functions reduced overreliance where explanations failed (N=199).

practice_claim: Require the reviewer to commit a judgment before seeing the agent's answer, or delay/slow the reveal at high-stakes checkpoints; aim these scrutiny mechanisms at the fast accept-loop where the programmer already 'knows' the plan, not uniformly across exploration-mode use.
boundary_conditions: Forcing reduced but did not eliminate overreliance; the most effective interventions were rated least favorable, and benefits accrued disproportionately to high Need-for-Cognition users. Acceleration/exploration split observed at suggestion level; transfer to autonomous-agent diffs untested.
citation: Shraddha Barke, Michael B. James, Nadia Polikarpova (2022). Grounded Copilot: How Programmers Interact with Code-Generating Models. arXiv:2206.15000.
claim_support: Grounded theory from 20 programmers: shallow validation concentrates in acceleration mode; exploration mode largely polices itself.

practice_claim: Model dependencies explicitly; let the scheduler fan out independent branches asynchronously; bound per-step time so one slow step cannot stall the batch.
boundary_conditions: Bounded per-step time must propagate a real error, not mask failure.
citation: Junwei Yu, Yepeng Ding, Hiroyuki Sato (2025). DynTaskMAS: A Dynamic Task Graph-driven Framework for Asynchronous and Parallel LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems. arXiv:2503.07675.
claim_support: Explicit dependency graphs with async fan-out and bounded per-step time outperform fixed schedules on heterogeneous agent work. Evidence audit: the identifier carried here, arXiv:2503.07675 (DynTaskMAS), measures its framework against serial execution on one seven-agent travel-planning workload, with no fixed-schedule baseline and no ablation of the task-graph component; the 21-33% figure is parallel-beats-serial, not dynamic-beats-fixed. Graded directional on that basis.

practice_claim: Re-query the repository with each generation draft (or exploration result) instead of retrieving once up front; let intermediate outputs sharpen the retrieval query.
boundary_conditions: Each iteration adds latency and cost; combine with a skip-retrieval policy so the loop runs only when retrieval is actually paying.
citation: Fengji Zhang, Bei Chen, Yue Zhang, Jacky Keung, Jin Liu, et al. (2023). RepoCoder: Repository-Level Code Completion Through Iterative Retrieval and Generation. arXiv:2303.12570.
claim_support: Iterative retrieval-generation beat single-shot RAG and in-file baselines by >10% on RepoEval.

practice_claim: Inject lightweight static-analysis facts (call graph, inheritance, configuration dependencies) as plain-text annotations in the agent's view of the code, primarily to stabilize navigation across runs.
boundary_conditions: Studied on one strong baseline (Codex) at roughly 10% more input tokens on medium-scale repositories; optimal annotation granularity and directionality depend on repository characteristics (dense-semantic repositories show diminishing returns, hub-heavy repositories benefit from inverse-only links). The residual value is variance reduction, so judge it on run-to-run metrics, not pass rate alone.
citation: Zhihao Lin, Mingyi Zhou, Yizhuo Yang, Li Li (2026). How Much Static Structure Do Code Agents Need? A Study of Deterministic Anchoring. arXiv:2606.26979.
claim_support: Static-structure annotations improve run-to-run stability (localization, trajectory, stability measured separately) more than raw capability.

practice_claim: Before reporting, gating, or rewarding on a pass rate, strengthen the oracle: augment hand-written benchmark tests with generated inputs (LLM- and mutation-based, coverage-driven, or random tests sampled against a trusted reference patch), synthesize plausible-but-wrong patches and keep the tests that kill them, and manually screen a sample of 'solved' instances for solution leakage and tests too weak to verify correctness. Then re-adjudicate all results, including existing leaderboard submissions and any acceptance gate or reward signal, under the stronger oracle.
boundary_conditions: Test generation needs a ground-truth implementation or trusted reference patch to differentiate against; augmentation is one-sided (catches more incorrect patches, cannot certify correctness); manual screening is labor-intensive and was done for one agent/model pair; strengthening covered only about half of instances, so the corrected rate is still an upper bound.
citation: Jiawei Liu, Chunqiu Steven Xia, Yuyao Wang, Lingming Zhang (2023). Is Your Code Generated by ChatGPT Really Correct? Rigorous Evaluation of Large Language Models for Code Generation. arXiv:2305.01210.
claim_support: HumanEval+ 80x test augmentation cut pass@k by up to ~19-29% across 26 models and reshuffled rankings — the weak oracle was mislabeling wrong code as correct.

practice_claim: When creating private eval sets, forbid annotators from copying any web or LLM source, require citation of inspiration sources, verify each prompt is not web-searchable, and disqualify items that fail originality/difficulty/ambiguity review.
boundary_conditions: Freshness decays from the day of release; leading models scored up to 43% lower on LBPP than HumanEval, so absolute scores are not comparable to legacy benchmarks; LBPP disqualified ~1/3 of proposed items, so budget for rejection.
citation: Alexandre Matton, Tom Sherborne, Dennis Aumiller, Elena Tommasone, Milad Alizadeh, et al. (2024). On Leakage of Code Generation Evaluation Datasets. arXiv:2407.07565.
claim_support: LBPP's anti-searchability protocol (no copying, cited inspirations, web-search verification, originality review) is the only construction defense against all three leakage channels including the synthetic-data channel.
